scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: Two reading stations
scenes.caption: Nikhil and Reva compare fictional request cards at stations. Group A contains typed cards; group B contains scans. The sorter makes 2 wrong category predictions in each group. Equal counts make the stations appear equally served.
scenes.speech: Nikhil and Reva compare fictional request cards at stations. Group A contains typed cards; group B contains scans. The sorter makes 2 wrong category predictions in each group. Equal counts make the stations appear equally served.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: Different group totals
scenes.caption: A has 20 test cards, while B has 5. Reva divides wrong predictions by each group’s own total. The fractions 2 out of 20 and 2 out of 5 describe different rates, despite equal error counts.
scenes.speech: A has 20 test cards, while B has 5. Reva divides wrong predictions by each group’s own total. The fractions 2 out of 20 and 2 out of 5 describe different rates, despite equal error counts.
scenes.dialogue: The denominator belongs to its group.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Name the measured error
scenes.caption: Error here means a predicted category differs from its checked label. No abstentions occur. These are overall error rates, not false alarm rates; the latter would need a positive category definition and a denominator counting negative cases.
scenes.speech: Error here means a predicted category differs from its checked label. No abstentions occur. These are overall error rates, not false alarm rates; the latter would need a positive category definition and a denominator counting negative cases.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: A tempting fairness badge
scenes.caption: A poster calls the sorter fair because both groups have 2 errors. Choose whether those counts justify the badge. The rate difference matters, but the tiny scanned sample cannot establish future outcomes or explain its cause.
scenes.speech: A poster calls the sorter fair because both groups have 2 errors. Choose whether those counts justify the badge. The rate difference matters, but the tiny scanned sample cannot establish future outcomes or explain its cause.
scenes.dialogue: Question the claim and its evidence.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Review the disagreement
scenes.caption: A disputed category goes to a teacher reviewer; an unreadable scan needs a clearer permitted copy. If the checked label itself is wrong, document its correction. Reva keeps these correction paths available without hiding records.
scenes.speech: A disputed category goes to a teacher reviewer; an unreadable scan needs a clearer permitted copy. If the checked label itself is wrong, document its correction. Reva keeps these correction paths available without hiding records.
scenes.dialogue: A person can challenge the output.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Evidence before a badge
scenes.caption: In the lab, calculate rates, identify missing evidence and assign reviews. Seek more representative tests and inspect error types. Keep sample sizes and limitations beside percentages; neither an isolated gap nor an equal result settles fairness for every use.
